topics.name: Reserved Runtime Roots
topics.purpose: Define reserved top-level AIGMos runtime roots as stable semantic namespaces whose concrete owners and module families are explicit and cannot be shadowed by user content.

semantics.reservation_rule: Reserved root identity cannot be redefined by user-installed modules or arbitrary mounts.
semantics.owner_rule: Each root resolves to one explicit semantic owner/family contract.
semantics.extension_rule: New reserved root requires explicit canonical contract and registry update.
semantics.shadow_rule: User/library content cannot shadow a reserved root by name/path coincidence.
semantics.lifecycle_rule: A reserved root may exist canonically even when the corresponding optional subsystem is disabled/unavailable.
semantics.authority_rule: Reserved status is naming/address-space protection, not elevated runtime authority.

invariants.rule: Runtime symbol namespaces, roots, mounts and dynamic families are explicit, collision-free and never inferred solely from filesystem layout or display labels.

hard_gates.condition: new reserved root appears without registry contract
disabled subsystem causes canonical reserved root identity to disappear where root is defined as persistent
reserved status interpreted as privileged authority
